text:
Lumen promised a launch in spring. A supplier strike delayed the launch until winter.

Lumen's managers hid failed tests. An engineer released the logs, and customers cancelled their orders.

To meet delivery promises, Lumen added rush orders. Rush orders displaced maintenance, so breakdowns caused further delays.

text:
Cedar's directors hid cancelled contracts. A clerk disclosed the cancellations, and lenders withdrew credit.

Cedar opened new depots to serve distant clients. Every new depot increased empty return trips, which drained funds needed for service.

Critics said Cedar hid losses until an audit exposed them. We reject that account: the audit found the losses were already disclosed.

This entirely fictional document is a teaching example.

text:
A rival claimed that Vale concealed failed orders until a technician revealed them and buyers fled.

We tested the rival's story. The dated notices showed that the orders had been disclosed before the technician spoke; we reject the concealment account.

text:
Moss added clients to cover fixed costs. Each client required a dedicated machine, so expansion raised fixed costs faster than revenue.

Moss removed a failed test from its brochure. A reviewer found the archived brochure, and customers asked for refunds.
